pr_body:
This PR adds support to statically link `sunmscapi`, required for the `sun_security_mscapi` package.

First of all, this still has a **critical issue** that needs to be taken care of before it would be ready to merge.
Additionally, some extra JNI configuration can be added, and the reachability handler can be refined.

The critical issue with this addition, happens when both `sunmscapi` and `sunec` are added:
`sunec.lib(ECC_JNI.obj) : error LNK2005: ThrowException already defined in sunmscapi.lib(security.obj)`

The offending definitions:
https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/0cbcc0176b3404262b95c180ea716e9b0cdeccf6/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp#L132
https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/0cbcc0176b3404262b95c180ea716e9b0cdeccf6/src/jdk.crypto.ec/share/native/libsunec/ECC_JNI.cpp#L50

I can handle the refinement of the reachability hander and the JNI config, but I need some help for the linking error.
pr_comments:
> The critical issue with this addition, happens when both `sunmscapi` and `sunec` are added:
`sunec.lib(ECC_JNI.obj) : error LNK2005: ThrowException already defined in sunmscapi.lib(security.obj)`

Unfortunately, this would have to be fixed in the JDK. However, `sunec` has been removed in JDK 16 (see [JDK-8235710](https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8235710)), so you could adjust the PR so that static linking is used only on JDK 16+, while on older JDKs we would continue to use dynamic linking (which will now work properly, see 5a34e716b111961e5a40e4c641ca3ba318d01ce5).

I added a bit more JNI stuff, not sure if that's desired or not. And I added the suggested check for jdk 16. I have yet to try it out locally as I can't seem to build a java 16 version of GraalVM locally.

My build fails on the generation of polybench.exe, which I don't think is required so I'm probalby building it wrong? What would be the correct mx command to get a simple native-image capable local build?
Managed to get the build working and was able to try it out. It should be ready for review now.

> Is this the entire JNI config? If not, would you be able to provide the rest?

I _think_ this is everything based on the source code I found [here](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/master/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp). The jdk 16 code seems to be identical as well.

The only thing that may be missing is [some exception classes](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/60e0ae5d1ada661540ca16388b3315580ebecc78/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp#L52-L60). But I'm not sure what to do with these.
Do I just put them in one entry like [here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/f07d5e3b858b2441e942958d8f329238ff0b0c87/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.hosted/src/com/oracle/svm/hosted/jdk/JNIRegistrationJava.java#L62-L69)?

> > Is this the entire JNI config? If not, would you be able to provide the rest?
> 
> I _think_ this is everything based on the source code I found [here](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/master/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp). The jdk 16 code seems to be identical as well.

Great, then we shouldn't need an agent to collect the `sunmscapi` config anymore.

> The only thing that may be missing is [some exception classes](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/60e0ae5d1ada661540ca16388b3315580ebecc78/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp#L52-L60). But I'm not sure what to do with these.
> Do I just put them in one entry like [here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/f07d5e3b858b2441e942958d8f329238ff0b0c87/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.hosted/src/com/oracle/svm/hosted/jdk/JNIRegistrationJava.java#L62-L69)?

I think we should register them here in a reachability handler, say `registerSunMSCAPIConfig`, which is triggered when the class `sun.security.mscapi.SunMSCAPI` becomes reachable. In fact, you can even move the registration of other handlers (suggested in https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/3300#discussion_r662244696) into this new handler instead of the helper method.

The config is now located in `registerSunMSCAPIConfig` which is registered as a reachabillity handler.
I duplicated the reachabillity handler for the linking, which could have 2 remarks:
* It duplicates the reachabillity handler, but I think it's clearer if the JNI config and the library linking are in separate methods
* I'm not sure if `registerClassInitializerReachabilityHandler` is right, or if it should be a normal class reachabillity handler.

Thank you for the feature, it was awaited for #1410 !

**Describe the issue**
I have a java program that read smart cards under linux. It uses sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11.
I have the following error when using PKCS11:
```
java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: sun.security.pkcs11.wrapper.PKCS11.connect(Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;)V [symbol: Java_sun_security_pkcs11_wrapper_PKCS11_connect or Java_sun_security_pkcs11_wrapper_PKCS11_connect__Ljava_lang_String_2Ljava_lang_String_2]
	at com.oracle.svm.jni.access.JNINativeLinkage.getOrFindEntryPoint(JNINativeLinkage.java:145)
	at com.oracle.svm.jni.JNIGeneratedMethodSupport.nativeCallAddress(JNIGeneratedMethodSupport.java:57)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.wrapper.PKCS11.connect(PKCS11.java)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.wrapper.PKCS11.<init>(PKCS11.java:147)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.wrapper.PKCS11.getInstance(PKCS11.java:160)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11.<init>(SunPKCS11.java:318)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11$1.run(SunPKCS11.java:112)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11$1.run(SunPKCS11.java:109)
	at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(AccessController.java:119)
	at sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11.configure(SunPKCS11.java:109)
...
```


**Steps to reproduce the issue**

compile and run this snippet with graal vm
```
    public static void main(String[] args)
    {
        String config = "name=opensc\n" //
            + "library=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/opensc-pkcs11.so\n" //
            + "slot=0\n";
        sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11 p11 = (SunPKCS11) new sun.security.pkcs11.SunPKCS11().configure("--" + config);

```


**Describe GraalVM and your environment:**
 - GraalVM version: graalvm-ce-java11-linux-20.1.0
 - JDK major version: 11
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS
 - Architecture: 64

$GRAALVMPATH/bin/java -agentlib:native-image-agent=config-merge-dir=$LINUX_CONFIG_DIR -jar test.jar -f ../testv3/v3.conf

3. As the PKCS11 class was initialized at build time, added this block of code in my program:
```
if (!nativeLoaded)
{
	nativeLoaded = true;
	try
	{
		Method m = Class.forName("sun.security.pkcs11.wrapper.PKCS11").getDeclaredMethod("initializeLibrary", new Class[] { boolean.class });
		System.loadLibrary("j2pkcs11");
		m.setAccessible(true);
		m.invoke(null, Boolean.FALSE);
	}
	catch (Throwable t)
	{
		t.printStackTrace();
	}
}
```

comments: @mttcr thank you for the report and for the in-depth investigation. It sounds like you succeeded in getting your program working with the method that you describe. I will look into statically linking this library in when needed, as we do with others.

Hello,
Thanks for your answer. Is there an approximate target version where j2pkcs11 and sunmscapi will be linked?

@mttcr to answer your question here, to keep the relevant information in the right place:

> could something similar be done to statically link j2pkcs11 under linux?

Yes normally that should be possible. PKCS11 does seem a bit bigger than SunMSCAPI, so it may be a bit more work.
All relevant code of PKCS11 can be found here: https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/tree/b988ca25875850ccb19218f52b12b38956c264e4/src/jdk.crypto.cryptoki

If you feel comfortable doing so, you could give it a shot yourself and open a PR?
It seems like there is both a windows and linux variant so it's probably best to add support for both platforms at once.

review_comments: These two should actually trigger the registration of `CPublicKey.of` instead of `CPrivateKey.of` (see [here](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/60e0ae5d1ada661540ca16388b3315580ebecc78/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp#L2506) and [here](https://github.com/graalvm/labs-openjdk-11/blob/60e0ae5d1ada661540ca16388b3315580ebecc78/src/jdk.crypto.mscapi/windows/native/libsunmscapi/security.cpp#L2590)).
